item.title: Man airlifted to Rochester after dirt bike crash
item.description: A 59-year-old man was taken by helicopter to St. Marys Hospital in Rochester Friday night after he reportedly crashed a dirt bike into a snowbank in the driveway of a home just outside of Alden.

item.title: Jeffery Lynn Swanson
item.description: Jeffery Lynn Swanson, 68, passed away on Tuesday, February 3, 2026, at his home in Albert Lea, MN, with his wife, Susan, by his side.

item.title: Jensen drops out of GOP race for Minnesota governor, will run for state auditor instead
item.description: Scott Jensen, the Republican nominee for Minnesota governor four years ago, has dropped out of this year’s contest and will run for state auditor instead.

item.title: Albert Lea Community Theatre to present the interactive musical comedy "Nunsense"
item.description: Albert Lea Community Theatre (ACT) continues its 60th season with the interactive musical comedy "Nunsense" at the Marion Ross Performing Arts Center, Feb. 19-28.

item.title: Stephen (“Steve”) Francis Schultz
item.description: Stephen (“Steve”) Francis Schultz, 72, passed away on Thursday, February 5, 2026. A funeral service will be held Friday, February 13, 2026, at St. Theodore’s Catholic Church at 2 PM with a reception in remembrance of Steve to follow at Marion Hall.

item.title: Jerome B "JB" Thompson
item.description: Died on February 2, 2026 in a hospital in Texas at the age of 83. He was the fourth child of Jewell and Lillian (Holstad) Thompson. He was born in Mason City, Iowa on April 17, 1942.

item.title: Carolyn Marcine Jenson
item.description: Carolyn Marcine Jenson was born 4/18/49 in Albert Lea, MN to Helmer and Margaret Whelan) Bergland.

item.title: Herman sworn in as 3rd ward councilor
item.description: Former Freeborn County Commissioner Ted Herman was sworn in Monday night as the new Third Ward Albert Lea city councilor to fill a vacancy left after the departure of former Councilor Jason Howland.

item.title: City approves first reading of amendment to cannabis ordinance; cap on dispensaries would increase to 4
item.description: The Albert Lea City Council on Monday approved the first reading of an amendment to the city’s ordinance surrounding cannabis and tobacco, including a change that would increase the number of cannabis retail registrations in the city from two to four.
